panels.description: Ammamma's home. Ammamma, worried, holding out her phone to Meera. SMS from "CureWell Billing".

lines.speaker: ammamma
lines.text: It knows my tablets, molay. It must be the hospital.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: It knows a lot. That's what worries me.

panels.description: Nyay appears beside the phone, worried.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Real details make a message feel genuine. They don't prove it is.

options.label: Call CureWell on the number printed on Ammamma's hospital card
Reply to the SMS and ask if it's genuine

panels.description: Close-up: Ammamma's thumb over "Pay now". Meera grabs the phone, surprised.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Wait! Don't tap that.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Never pay through a link in a message. If money has already gone, call 1930 or report it at cybercrime.gov.in straight away.

panels.description: Phone screen. Meera's reply and the answer.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Thirty minutes now?

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Rushing you is the oldest trick. Asking the sender proves nothing. Check through a number you already trust.

panels.description: Hospital reception. Meera on the phone, neutral. CureWell helpline.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Then how did a scammer get her prescriptions?

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Six days. And nobody told Ammamma?

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Once a company knows its data has leaked, it must tell everyone affected, and the Data Protection Board, without delay.

options.label: Post the scam SMS and the news on social media, tagging CureWell
Write to CureWell's Data Protection Officer, using the contact on its website

panels.description: Meera's post with hundreds of shares. Zoomed in: the screenshot shows Ammamma's name and medicines.
Ammamma's home. Ammamma, worried, on a call.

lines.speaker: ammamma
lines.text: Molay, my cousin in Dubai saw my tablets on the internet!

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Your post put Ammamma's details in front of even more people. Pushing CureWell is fair. Spreading her data isn't.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: I'll take it down.

panels.description: Phone screen: CureWell's message to Ammamma.
panels.caption: Next morning.

panels.description: Ammamma's home. Meera reading, neutral; Ammamma beside her, worried.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: It says everything it should. Just six days late.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: And that last line? MediStack did the work. CureWell still answers for it.

options.label: Save the notice and write to the DPO asking exactly which of Ammamma's records were exposed

panels.description: Office. Arjun at his desk, neutral.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: We ran a breach drill at work last month. Lock it down, tell the Board straight away, send the Board a full report within 72 hours, and tell every affected user without delay.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Could CureWell have stopped this?

panels.description: Arjun, happy, counting on his fingers.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: There are minimum safeguards. Encrypt the data. Control who can get in. Keep access logs and actually check them. Keep backups. And put security terms in the vendor's contract.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: An open folder of readable records fails more than one of those.

panels.description: Only if asked_for_details. Phone screen: the DPO's reply.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: At least we know exactly what's out there.

panels.description: Ammamma's home. Ammamma, neutral, with a cup of tea.

lines.speaker: ammamma
lines.text: Will anyone pay me for all this worry?

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: The Board can fine CureWell up to ₹250 crore for weak security, and up to ₹200 crore for telling people late. But that money goes to the government.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: So Ammamma gets nothing?

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: She gets answers and safer systems. And once CureWell reported the breach, the Board can order it to fix things fast.

scam_sms.text: Dear patient Saraswathi, your insurance claim for Metformin and Amlodipine was rejected. Pay ₹4,999 within 1 hour or your treatment will stop:

messages.text: Yes madam, 100% genuine. Pay in 30 minutes or treatment stops.

curewell_helpline.text: Madam, we never ask for payment by SMS. That message is fraud. But we are not aware of any data problem.

news_headline.text: Navpur hospital chain's patient records found exposed online. The security researcher who found them says she alerted the hospital on 9 July.

embed.text: Dear patient Saraswathi, your insurance claim for Metformin and Amlodipine was rejected. Pay ₹4,999 within 1 hour or your treatment will stop:

breach_notice.title: Important: a data breach affecting your records.

sections.heading: What happened:
sections.text: Between 2 and 9 July 2027, a storage folder at MediStack, the company that hosts our patient records, was left open online. It held the names, phone numbers, appointment dates and prescription details of about 18,000 patients, including yours. We learned of it on 9 July.

sections.heading: What this may mean for you:
sections.text: You may get fake messages or calls that use your details to ask for money.

sections.heading: What we have done:
sections.text: MediStack locked the folder on 9 July. We have tightened who can access our records, and we have informed the Data Protection Board.

sections.heading: What you can do:
sections.text: CureWell will never ask you to pay through an SMS link. Call us only on the number on your hospital card. If you lose money, call 1930 or report it at cybercrime.gov.in.

sections.heading: Please note:
sections.text: this breach happened at MediStack, our vendor, not at CureWell.

dpo_reply.body: For Mrs Saraswathi, the exposed records were: name, phone number, two appointment dates and her prescription list. No payment or ID details were included. Questions: dpo@curewell.example.

episode4_teaser.text: Episode 4: Under 18. Who decides what Kabir shares?

CS11.question: A message names your real medicines and asks you to pay. Does that prove it's from your hospital?
options: Yes, only the hospital would know that
CS11.explanation: Leaked data makes scams look real. Check through a number you already trust, and if you lose money, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in.

LS12.question: A researcher alerted CureWell on 9 July. By 15 July, no patient has been told. Is CureWell in breach of its intimation duty?
shortAnswerOptions: No, it only has to tell the Board
LS12.modelAnswer: Yes. The open folder is a "personal data breach" under s. 2(u), which covers accidental disclosure or loss of access, not just proven misuse. s. 8(6) requires intimation to the Board and each affected Data Principal. Rule 7(1) requires CureWell, on becoming aware, to tell each affected patient without delay, to the best of its knowledge. The 72 hours in Rule 7(2)(b) apply only to the detailed report to the Board, and Rule 7(2)(a) requires an initial report to the Board without delay. Failing to give notice falls under Schedule item 2: up to ₹200 crore.

CS12.question: Meera posted screenshots showing Ammamma's medicines to shame the hospital. Was that a good idea?
options: No, it spread Ammamma's details even further
CS12.explanation: Push the company through its Data Protection Officer or grievance contact, not by sharing the person's data.

CS13.question: After a breach, the company's message to you must include:
options: What happened, how it could affect you, what they're doing, what you can do, and who to contact
Nothing. Companies only have to tell the government
CS13.explanation: You must be told all of this clearly, in plain language, without delay.

LS13.question: CureWell's notice says the breach was MediStack's fault. Does that shift legal responsibility to MediStack?
LS13.modelAnswer: No. Under s. 8(1) the Data Fiduciary is responsible for compliance, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary, for processing done by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor. s. 8(5) requires safeguards covering processing by its processors, s. 8(2) allows processors only under a valid contract, and Rule 6(1)(f) requires that contract to provide for reasonable security safeguards. CureWell may have a contractual claim against MediStack, but it answers to the Board.

LS14.question: Leaving timing aside, does the content of CureWell's notice meet Rule 7(1)?
LS14.modelAnswer: Yes. Rule 7(1) requires, in concise, clear and plain language: (a) a description of the breach, including its nature, extent and timing; (b) likely consequences for her; (c) mitigation measures taken or being taken; (d) safety measures she can take; and (e) contact details of someone who can answer her questions. The notice covers all five, and was sent to her registered phone. Its weakness is timing (see LS12) and the misleading line about responsibility (see LS13).

CS14.question: After discovering a breach, how long does a company have to give the Data Protection Board the full details?
CS14.explanation: It must alert the Board straight away, then send the full report within 72 hours.

LS15.question: Which minimum safeguards in Rule 6(1) bear most directly on a storage folder left open online?
shortAnswerOptions: Encryption, access control and access logging
A privacy policy on the website
LS15.modelAnswer: Rule 6(1) sets minimums: (a) encryption, obfuscation, masking or virtual tokens; (b) access control over computer resources; (c) logs, monitoring and review to detect unauthorised access; (d) backups for continued processing; (e) keeping logs and personal data for one year for detection and investigation; (f) security terms in the processor contract; and (g) technical and organisational measures. Readable records in an open folder suggest failures of (a), (b) and (c). Under Rule 7(2)(b), the detailed report to the Board is due within 72 hours of becoming aware, or longer if the Board allows it on a written request. Failing to take reasonable safeguards under s. 8(5) is Schedule item 1: up to ₹250 crore.

CS15.question: If the Board fines CureWell, who gets the money?
CS15.explanation: Penalties go to the government. The DPDP Act doesn't pay compensation to the people affected.

LS16.question: Ammamma's leaked records include her prescriptions. Does the DPDP Act give health data extra protection as a special category?
LS16.modelAnswer: No. Unlike GDPR Art. 9, the DPDP Act has no separate category of sensitive personal data. But when setting a penalty, the Board must consider "the type and nature of the personal data affected" (s. 33(2)(b)), along with the other s. 33(2) factors. On receiving CureWell's breach intimation, the Board can direct urgent remedial or mitigation measures and inquire (s. 27(1)(a)). Penalties go to the Consolidated Fund of India (s. 34); the Act gives the patient no compensation. s. 44(2)(a) of the Act also omits s. 43A of the IT Act, the old compensation route for negligent security, once that provision is in force.

CF14.title: What counts as a breach
CF14.plain: Any leak, loss, or unauthorised use of your data counts, even by accident and even if no one has misused it yet.

CF15.title: You must be told
CF15.plain: After a breach, the company must tell you what happened, how it affects you, what it's doing, what you can do, and who to contact, without delay.

help.title: Real-world help
help.text: If you lose money to a scam, call the National Cyber Crime Helpline on 1930 or report it at cybercrime.gov.in

CF16.title: Blaming the vendor
CF16.plain: A company is responsible for its vendors. If a vendor leaks your data, the company still answers for it.

CF17.title: Locks, logs and 72 hours
CF17.plain: Companies must encrypt data, control access, keep and check logs, and keep backups. After a breach, they must alert the Board at once and report fully within 72 hours.

CF18.title: Penalties, not payouts
CF18.plain: Fines can reach ₹250 crore for weak security and ₹200 crore for late notice. The money goes to the government, not to you.

endings.title: Shared too widely
endings.caption: CureWell is fixing its systems, but Meera's post spread Ammamma's details further.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Next time, push the company, not the person's data.

card.title: What to do instead
items: Check messages through a number you already trust.
Write to the company's Data Protection Officer.
If money is lost, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in.

endings.title: Well handled
endings.caption: Ammamma is safe from the scam, and Meera has CureWell's breach notice saved.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: You checked, you asked, and you kept the proof. If CureWell drags its feet, you're ready for the Board.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Ammamma's safe. But without the notice, you'd have nothing to show the Board later.
